independent_review.verbatim:
**Independent verdict: one distinct source-only candidate.** The candidate is the Guardian’s **exposure-dependent placement rule**. Under the default predicate, an otherwise eligible sky-exposed position passes **1 of 20** draws, while a sky-hidden position passes **20 of 20**. The shared sky helper and the surrounding spawn machinery carry no separate credit. [Guardian predicate](/Users/a15356015027/Desktop/dynasty/tools/cod4/legacy-migration-acceptance/.work/sources/minecraft-forge-1.20.1-47.4.10/net/minecraft/world/entity/monster/Guardian.java:296)

- **Sea-level projection.** `LevelReader.java:88–106` checks sky light directly at or above sea level. Below it, the helper first checks the same X/Z at sea level, then scans the blocks strictly between that plane and the candidate. A block stops the projection when `getLightBlock(...) > 0` and `!blockstate.liquid()`. The candidate block is outside the scan. `BlockAndTintGetter.java:22–24` defines the direct check as sky brightness reaching the maximum light level. [Projection source](/Users/a15356015027/Desktop/dynasty/tools/cod4/legacy-migration-acceptance/.work/sources/minecraft-forge-1.20.1-47.4.10/net/minecraft/world/level/LevelReader.java:88)
- **Exception and limits.** `Guardian.java:296–298` draws `nextInt(20)` first. Zero skips the sky helper only. Non-Peaceful difficulty and water below still apply, and `NATURAL` still requires water at the candidate. I independently reproduced all seven authored synthetic case outcomes. Those are callback results at fixed positions, with selection, Forge arbitration, collision, and admission still separate. Monument selection, Elder Guardian marker placement, inherited Forge placement, and generic water checks add no credit. [Candidate and cases](/Users/a15356015027/Desktop/dynasty/docs/cod4/audit-20261022/ecology-availability-research/general-guardian-underwater-sky-native-placement-source-review-20261126.json:210)

EA-0007 invokes the same named helper as a **hard configured veto**, with its rarity roll applied separately (`MowzieEntity.java:147–151,206–212`). Guardian instead makes the roll waive only the exposure veto, giving open and screened sites different pass rates under one rule. The earlier Elder Guardian review included the exact complete `Guardian.java:1–473`, including the callback. Its semantic decision covered fatigue recipients, effect admission, and packet feedback. The prior beam review covered combat and presentation. Neither decision owned this placement policy.
